experiment: Parallel native code generation from already normally O3-optimized LLVM IR
primary_candidate: llvm-split fixed8; eight independent Clang IR backend commands scheduled by Ninja -j4; numeric native merge with ld.lld -r -O0; exact promoted-definition localization
secondary_pilot: LLD full-LTO reader with lto-O0/lto-CGO3/8partitions; not proposed integration because private binding and worker-pool issues require explicit handling
source_changes: none; original baseline CHECKER source and all other original baseline objects
configuration: x86-64 scalar Release-g0; exact normal frontend -O3 flags; no -flto prelink frontend optimization
measurement_status: Diagnostic cloud timings only; not controlled paired hardware performance evidence

bounded_environment_limit.cause: Test formats /proc/<getpid()>/exe, but managed execution uses namespace PIDs with host /proc; direct /proc/self/exe and explicit executable paths work

limitations: No authoritative throughput or build-speed conclusion from cloud timings
Split backend changes machine code/layout; only unsplit IR roundtrip is byte-identical
Single scalar Release-g0 CHECKER proof; vector, debug, sanitizer, PGO and multiple-heavy-TU integration belong to subsequent validation
Final binary grows in nonloaded ELF symbol and string tables; no code/data allocation growth
Backend-only diagnostic source-location fidelity requires its separate tiny inline-assembly negative check
Original LLD pilot did not establish an actual eight-partition worker cap from --threads=4; primary Ninja candidate caps backend commands directly

The isolated backend command omitted -Wall/-Werror; production integration now mirrors these flags. Reviewer confirmed invalid assembly still fails but original C location precision is lost after IR serialization.
